newsitem.title: USA: Florida House votes to outlaw 'date rape' drug.
newsitem.headline: Florida House votes to outlaw 'date rape' drug.

text.p: Florida's House of Representatives voted to outlaw the drug Rohypnol on Thursday, saying the so-called "date rape" drug had no therapeutic use and was becoming the drug of choice of sexual predators.
The drug has come under fire from law enforcement officials who say sex crime victims unknowingly ingest it, often becoming incapacitated and losing their memories of the event.
"This is the single most significant protection for women that we'll pass this year," said Representative Ken Pruitt., R-Port St. Lucie, and a principal sponsor of the bill.

The bill changes the drug's classification from a Schedule IV to Schedule I drug, a group that includes marijuana, cocaine and LSD. It also will need to be passed by the state Senate before becoming law.
Three other states, Idaho, Minnesota and Oklahoma, have outlawed the drug.

Manufactured by Hoffman-LaRoche Inc., the drug is widely used in Europe and Latin America for sleep disorders. About 10 times more potent than Valium, it is believed to be smuggled into the United States from Mexico and Colombia.
Hoffman-LaRoche is a U.S. affiliate of Swiss pharmaceutical group Roche Holding Ltd..
Last year, U.S. lawmakers stiffened penalties for misuse of the drug, but retained its legal status.
